clue.text: One wearing short garment sits oddly, being extremely uneasy

indicators.note: the garment wears the 'one', so the letter goes inside it
short means the garment's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a jumper is a knitted pullover garment
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: oddly means take the first and third letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone in a skimpy outfit, sitting awkwardly, feels very ill at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims JUMPER to JUMPE; 'wearing' puts I inside to give JUMPIE; 'oddly' takes S and T from 'sits'. JUMPER is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpy means nervous, and its superlative describes someone most nervous of all.

clue.text: Little woman given part in play a tragic queen

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in the novel Little Women
an actor given a part in a play has been cast

explanation.surface: A small woman lands the role of a doomed queen in a stage tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocasta, mother and wife of Oedipus in Greek tragedy, is the queen whose fate is tragic.

clue.text: Helper working in farmyard? Not right

indicators.note: working signals the letters being worked into a new order
not means the letter for right is left out of the word

explanation.surface: A hired hand toils on the farm, though something is not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' drops one R from FARMYARD, leaving FAMYARD (with one R still in it); 'working' rearranges those letters with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Man Friday, the servant in Robinson Crusoe, became the general term for a loyal assistant.

clue.text: One father about to make a saint

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: about means the father's word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father
to do is to make, as in do a drawing

explanation.surface: A priest is on the point of turning someone into a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Isidore of Seville is a canonised scholar, so the name is an instance of a saint.

clue.text: Depicter of Crucifixion's run out into town

indicators.note: out means the letter for run is removed from the name

parts.note: Sir John Stainer composed the oratorio The Crucifixion, which depicts it in music; with the possessive S
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A painter of the Crucifixion is run out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a painter, but Stainer depicted the Crucifixion in music. STAINES is a town on the Thames west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Staines is a riverside town in Surrey, so it is a specific example of a town.

clue.text: Twin characters self-consciously stylish.

indicators.note: twin means the same piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: chi is a character of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Two identical figures are trying rather hard to look fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi describes something pretentiously or affectedly elegant, chic with too much effort showing.

clue.text: Anti-nuclear group limiting test over US city

indicators.note: limiting means the group's letters enclose the other piece on both sides

parts.note: CND is the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament

indicators.note: over in this down clue means the exam is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: an A level is a British school-leaving exam

explanation.surface: Protesters against nuclear weapons cordon off a site after a weapons test in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the exam backwards; A levels are the exams English pupils take at about eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleveland, in Ohio, is a large city of the United States.

clue.text: Understanding fashionable view

parts.note: something in fashion is in
a sight is a view, something seen

explanation.surface: Being trendy means seeing things a certain way.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep understanding of a person or situation, a near synonym.

clue.text: Having put away nothing, it's more snip difficult for saver

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Having put away nothing, it's more snip difficult for saver' has a stray OCR word 'snip' (O in HARDER); removing it exceeds the OCR-misread limit and the scan is blank
annotationWithheld.clue: Having put away nothing, it's more snip difficult for saver

clue.text: Read inconclusively about Russian ruler and Conservative working in cahoots

indicators.note: about means the reading word goes around the ruler and the party letter
inconclusively means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully, so read in the past is conned
Ivan the Terrible was a ruler of Russia

explanation.surface: Someone skims a report on a tsar and a Tory plotting together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read' looks present tense but is the past tense of con, to study; 'inconclusively' drops its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Connivance is secret cooperation in wrongdoing, which is what working in cahoots means.

clue.text: Ambitious contract in spades leading to game? East goes off

indicators.note: leading to puts the spades letter in front of the rest

parts.note: S is the card-game abbreviation for spades

indicators.note: goes off means the compass letter departs from the word

parts.note: game means lame, as in a game leg

explanation.surface: A bridge player bids high in spades, but East leaves the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all bridge, yet 'game' means lame, as in a game leg. LAME loses E.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a slam is a bid to win all or all but one of the tricks, the most ambitious contract.

clue.text: Actor judging his role badly written

indicators.note: badly written means the letters are set down in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A critic panning an actor's performance in a poorly scripted part.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Gielgud was a celebrated English stage and film actor.

clue.text: Deal with a daughter's style of clothing

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
dress means a style of clothing, as in evening dress

explanation.surface: Handling a girl's choice of outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to tackle or deal with it.

clue.text: Family members work hard to support son's operation

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting below, so the son's letter comes on top

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
kin are one's relatives
graft is British slang for hard work

explanation.surface: Relatives put in long hours to pay for a boy's surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin graft is a surgical operation transplanting skin from one area to another.

clue.text: Plant within my control

indicators.note: within means the plant's name sits inside the other word

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A gardener boasts that a plant is under their command.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastery is command or control over something, a close synonym.

clue.text: Detailed leader of European party to make speech

indicators.note: leader of means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Lab is short for the British Labour Party
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: The head of a European party is due to give an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate and full of detail, so detailed is a synonym.

clue.text: Lady pulls out of musical film, keeping a quarter of the capital

indicators.note: keeping means the remaining words hold the other piece inside
pulls out of means that word leaves the film's title

parts.note: My Fair Lady is a musical film based on Pygmalion

explanation.surface: An actress withdraws from a musical while holding on to a share of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulls out of' takes LADY from MY FAIR LADY, leaving MY FAIR; 'keeping' puts A inside. MAYFAIR is an upmarket district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayfair is a district of London, the capital, so it is one of its quarters.

clue.text: A learner gets 50%: needs support for study in class

parts.note: L is the learner abbreviation, from British L-plates

indicators.note: 50% means take the first half of the next word

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A pupil scrapes half marks and needs help in a school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics studied in school classes.

clue.text: Kick a child who's loving and giving?

parts.note: in the rhyme Monday's Child, Friday's child is loving and giving, so this is Fri's, short for Friday's
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Who would kick a child so affectionate and generous?
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme says 'Friday's child is loving and giving'; Fri is the usual abbreviation for Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a thrill or sudden shiver of excitement, which is a kick.

clue.text: Weirdo disturbed bold lad

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A strange, troubled young man with a forward manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is an eccentric or strange person, the same as a weirdo.

clue.text: Sort of illusion Capitol has been rebuilt?

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a different order

explanation.surface: Is the restored Capitol building a trick of the eye?
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is a trick of vision, so the word describes that kind of illusion.

clue.text: Say colour blue seen to fade

indicators.note: say means the word for colour is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to dye is to colour
blue means sad or down

explanation.surface: Someone notices a blue colour fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: To die down is to fade or subside gradually.

clue.text: Recklessly spend pounds on a turn to buy drinks

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
a shout is someone's turn to buy a round, in British and Australian slang

explanation.surface: Spending freely, with money down for someone's round at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A SHOUT is British and Australian slang for one's turn to buy a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is informal for spending money extravagantly.

clue.text: Deceased pet lover's estate may be deteriorating thus?

definitions.text: Deceased pet lover's estate may be
definitions.meaning: a dog lover's fortune may be bequeathed to the dogs

explanation.surface: A dead animal lover's fortune is left to the pets, and wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means declining badly, while literally an estate may pass to dogs in a will.

clue.text: Bird nesting in hibiscus

indicators.note: nesting in means the bird sits inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A bird has made its nest in a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: Real Madrid fan?

parts.note: a supporter of the Spanish football club, or a genuine fan in Madrid, using the Spanish word for an enthusiast

explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for an enthusiast, especially of bullfighting, means a keen fan or devotee.

clue.text: Old comic found in drawer?

definitions.meaning: A British boys' weekly paper featuring Billy Bunter
something that draws things towards it, an attractor

explanation.surface: An old comic book discovered in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' suggests furniture, but here it is something that draws, as iron is drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron-attracting bar draws metal towards it, and the same name belonged to an old British story paper.

clue.text: Film director shut out for making loud noise

indicators.note: out here means the shut word sits outside the director's name

parts.note: pent means shut in, as in pent up
Fritz Lang directed the film Metropolis

explanation.surface: A director is shut out of the studio for being too noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a sound that is loud and resonant, often mournful.
